sections.overview: The seven-spot ladybird is a familiar predatory beetle.
sections.identification: Adults usually have red wing cases with seven black spots; other species can resemble them.
sections.habitat: It lives on vegetation in gardens, parks and woodland edges.
sections.diet: Aphids are its main prey, although it can also take other small invertebrates and supplementary foods.
sections.behavior: Both larvae and adults hunt on plants, and adults shelter in protected places during winter.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on plants near prey; larvae hatch and pass through several growth stages before pupating.
sections.ecology: By consuming aphids, it is a predator in plant-based food webs and can contribute to natural pest control.
sections.conservation: The Woodland Trust describes it as common in Britain and not a UK species of conservation concern; this is not a global assessment.
